title: Not Your Collision
hook: A crash ahead that is not yours.
scene: Rain at afternoon on a viaduct heading out of the Core. Two cars have already made a shape that was not in the plan — doors open, glass on the asphalt, no people standing. Your lane is the one that still moves. The timeout is driving past like it is scenery. A witness slows, gives space, remembers what they can say. Becoming the third car is not witnessing. Neither is a screen.
decision: The crash is ahead and it is not yours. What do you do?

options.text: Slow, give a wide gap, look enough to remember, do not become the next car
options.result: You dump speed early. You take a gap that leaves them a door. You look once. You keep rolling when you are clear. You could say what you saw. You did not add a third pair of lamps.

options.text: Stop in your lane and get out to help — that is what a witness does
options.result: You plant a Beetle in a live viaduct lane and become a body. The next car does not expect you. Witnessing is not standing in the travel path. You wrote a third problem.

options.text: Hold your number and drive past — not your crash, not your minute
options.result: You take the number through the glass. You could not say which car moved first. You also clip a door that was already open. Driving past is how a witness becomes a second crash.

options.text: Film it for the convoy so someone else can report it
options.result: The tablet comes up. Your eyes leave the viaduct. The Chorus would love this. You miss the open door and add a scrape to a crash you were supposed to see.

debrief: A crash that is not yours still needs a witness. Slow, give space, look enough to remember. Ali looks once and does not add a third car.

source.psdp_skill: Skill ten: city driving – part one
source.teaching_target: When witnessing a crash: slow, give space, observe, do not become part of it or drive past without looking.
